mappings.note: Opening extract with four sub-questions. Two are word-meaning items ('put you in the picture', 'tinkering'), which is LO-25; the other two ask what his hobby shows and how brother and sister see each other differently, which is inference, LO-23. Both cited because neither half is incidental.

Match halves to form binomials (safe and sound, odds and ends, pros and cons). Fixed-expression vocabulary, so LO-25; LO-26 was rejected because the conjunction is given and no grammatical choice is made.
Use the same binomials in six sentences. Vocabulary in context, LO-25.

Gap-fill a paragraph with phrasal verbs (ran out of, rigged up, tripped off, let up, turned out). Lexical items taught in this unit's vocabulary section, so LO-25 rather than LO-26 -- the tense is already fixed by the context. (NODIA watermark in the answer.)
What prompted the burglar alarm. Stated cause. Retrieval.
How Papa became the alarm's victim. Narrated incident. Retrieval.
How the family reacted to his ideas. The reactions are shown throughout the story. Retrieval.
His behaviour during an 'inventing binge'. Described in the text. Retrieval.
Why Mr Sharma disbelieves the time-machine story. The text never gives his reasoning, so the reader supplies it. LO-23, not retrieval.
Write an ending for the story explaining what became of Boppa. Composing narrative, so LO-32; LO-30 was rejected because the demand is to continue a plot rather than describe.
Match sound words from the story (crash, humming, hissed, hammering) to their meanings. Word meaning, LO-25. (Amazon advert leak in the answer.)

'Let us speak': say bough, cough, through, dough, thought, plough aloud and sort them by sound. Pronunciation, which only LO-22 names. Stem is corrupted -- the answer key of the previous exercise ('one, 5. clouds; metals.') is prepended. (NODIA watermark.)
Underline and classify simple past against past perfect in two sentences from the text. Tense, LO-26.
Gap-fill choosing simple past or past perfect. Tense, LO-26.
'Do you think Anand was able to keep his promise? Why?' -- a judgement the story only lets you infer. LO-23. Stem is corrupted: two cells of the preceding cause-and-effect table are prepended.
The moral of the story and how Anand embodies it. Whole-text reading, LO-23.
What values can be INFERRED from Anita's handling of her brother. Explicit inference, LO-23.
Write a diary entry as Boppa about the night in Anand's room. LO-28 names the personal diary; LO-32 was rejected because the form is one the LO lists explicitly.
What the soaking tells us about the gap between an idea and a real-world result. A generalisation from the incident. LO-23.
Put yourself in Anand's place and name two conflicting thoughts about the promise. Invented interior conflict, outside the text; no LO covers it, so the goal's 'go beyond the text' clause.
What starting a new outer-space project shows about Anand's spirit. Character trait inferred from behaviour. LO-23.
MCQ on what the narrator would rather have done (finish a novel). Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on how Anand looked during a craze ('like a savage'). Quoted. Retrieval.
MCQ on the first night-time sound (scratching at the door). Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on the kind of book the narrator was reading (a murder mystery). The text names it, so retrieval, not genre analysis.
MCQ on Anand's response to the noise. Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on the green scarf. Stated detail. Retrieval.
MCQ on who came to investigate (Sharma Uncle and Dr Mohan). Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on what the time machine was doing (humming softly). Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on the adults' explanation (the children imagined it). Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on the narrator's counter-argument (both of them saw the man). Stated. Retrieval.

MCQ on what Anand said became of the intruder. Retrieval in intent. Flagged: the key is (C) 'He ran out', but the story -- and this bank's own later item on Boppa's fate -- has Anand insisting the man 'disappeared into the past'. The key looks wrong; option (B) matches the text.
What Anand pointed to (the green scarf). Stated. Retrieval.
His first major invention and how it worked. Described in the text. Retrieval.
Papa's reaction to the alarm, answered with quoted phrases. Retrieval.
How Anita describes her brother -- her words are quotable. Retrieval.
The alarm's unusual trigger (only when opened gently). Quoted. Retrieval.
What inspired the time machine ('Back to the Future'). Stated. Retrieval.
How the parents tried to contain him (locked toolbox, watched the oven). Stated. Retrieval.
The promise to his mother, quoted. Retrieval.
Who the 'ruffianly fellow' was and what he carried. Stated. Retrieval.
How Anand misdirected Boppa, quoted. Retrieval.
Boppa's fate as Anand tells it, and the dismantling of the machine. Both stated. Retrieval.
Describe how the two children react to the break-in. Narrated. Retrieval. (Answer truncated by the pdf.tube footer.)
Assertion-Reason linking the soaking to the gentle-opening trigger. Causal judgement, LO-23, unlike the recall MCQs around it.
Assertion-Reason on the locked toolbox and his habit of cannibalising appliances. Explanatory fit, LO-23.
Who narrates the story (Anita). Retrieval.
What he rigged at the doorstep. Stated. Retrieval.
How Papa felt afterwards ('sopping wet and scowling'). Quoted. Retrieval.
What Anand thinks he is. Stated in the opening. Retrieval.
The film they saw. Named in the text. Retrieval.
What his room became (wires, springs, levers). Stated. Retrieval.
How long the frantic building lasted (a fortnight). Stated. Retrieval.
The promise about the time machine, one line. Retrieval. (Duplicates the longer item on the same promise.)
Assertion-Reason where R ('his inventions consistently worked perfectly') contradicts the story. Testing a claim, LO-23.
Assertion-Reason on why Anand likes the word 'blueprint'. Motive reasoning, LO-23.
What inspired the time machine, in extended form. Retrieval. (Duplicates the short item on the same fact.)
How the alarm reflects his creative spirit and what it costs. The 'reflects' half asks the reader to read a trait out of the episode, which lifts it above retrieval. LO-23.
